title: Annotatio IV §.XVI: Peter de Bruis, Waldo, Arnold — true Supper doctrine disseminated; Waldenses named
pass_a_gloss: As the Age progressed, PETER DE BRUIS and a certain Henry the Monk, in various parts of Gaul, and a little later PETER WALDO Citizen of Lyons, with a certain Arnold as companion, in the Cities of Lyons and Albi, disseminated far and wide by preaching the true doctrine even concerning the Sacred Supper — their Followers called from partly their names, partly the cities in which they taught: Petrobrusians, Arnoldists, Waldenses, Poor of Lyons, Albigenses — weighed down by innumerable calumnies from Roman Pontiffs’ flatterers, which yet Our men most effectively wiped away and washed off as often as they arose, and among these the most learned Armachanus in the often-cited Book on the Succession and State of the Western Churches.
pass_b_english: Later in the age PETER DE BRUIS and Henry the Monk, then PETER WALDO of Lyons with Arnold, preached the true Supper doctrine across Gaul — Lyons and Albi.
Followers called Petrobrusians, Arnoldists, Waldenses, Poor of Lyons, Albigenses — buried under papal flatterers’ calumnies that Our writers (Armachanus among the ablest) repeatedly washed off.
source_text: Progressu Seculi, PETRUS DE BRUIS & Henricus quidam Monachus, in variis Galliæ partibus, pauloque post, PETRUS WALDUS Civis Lugdunensis, cum quodam Arnoldo socio, in Civitatibus Lugdunensi & Albigensi, veram, etiam de S. Cœna doctrinam, longè latèque prædicando disseminarunt, Sequacibus, ab istorum partim, partim à civitatum, in quibus illi docuêre, nominibus, Petro-Bruisiani, Arnoldistæ, Waldenses seu Waldenses, Pauperes de Lugduno, Albienses seu Albigenses appellatis, innumerisque à Pontificum Rom. assentatoribus, gravatis calumniis, quas tamen Nostrates efficacissimè toties quoties absterserunt ac diluerunt, interque hos doctissimus Armachanus, Libro sæpiùs citato de Success. ac Stat. Eccles. Occidentalium.
